pr.title: Check that the ABI of the instance we are inlining is correct
pr.description:
When computing the `CallSite` in the mir inliner, double check that the instance of the function that we are inlining is compatible with the signature from the trait definition that we acquire from the MIR.

Fixes #120940

r? @oli-obk or @cjgillot

processing.reason: The historical regression is a compile-time MIR-inliner bug: on an `InstanceDef::Item` associated function whose own ABI differs from the trait-definition-derived `fn_sig`, the pre-fix inliner formed a `CallSite` and inlined using the incompatible signature, leading to a `validate_types` ICE. The fixed compiler instead rejects the underlying trait impl with E0053 (`expected "rust-call" fn, found "C" fn`). The historical test is therefore a compile-fail UI test, not a program with a different defined runtime value. Any source program that actually exercises the ABI-mismatched `Fn::call` implementation is rejected by the modern compiler and cannot pass Miri; modeling the inliner's `Some(CallSite)` versus `None` decision as an ordinary value-returning function would be a meta-level restatement of the patch, not the original program semantics, and forcing a runtime difference via ABI transmutes or invented calling conventions would be an unrelated/UB rewrite. Thus no source-grounded original/transformed pair can be validated under Miri for this compile-fail/ICE fix.

analysis.originalLogic: The MIR inliner built a `CallSite` for a callee by resolving the called `def_id`, computing `let fn_sig = self.tcx.fn_sig(def_id).instantiate(self.tcx, args);`, and returning `Some(CallSite { callee, fn_sig, block: bb, source_info })` without comparing that signature against the actual instance's own function signature/ABI.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical inliner selected and inlined an `InstanceDef::Item` call when the callee's instance signature ABI did not match the ABI of the signature obtained from the trait definition in MIR, even though it was about to use the trait-definition-derived `fn_sig` for the `CallSite`. The fix adds an `AssocFn` guard and computes `instance_fn_sig` from `instance_def_id`; if `instance_fn_sig.abi() != fn_sig.abi()`, it must `return None` instead of inlining. This is a missing compatibility precondition, not an invented alternate rewrite.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR call sites considered by the inliner where `callee.def` is `InstanceDef::Item(instance_def_id)` and `def_kind(instance_def_id) == DefKind::AssocFn`, especially trait method implementations such as `Fn`, `FnMut`, and `FnOnce` implementations whose instance ABI differs from the expected trait ABI (`extern "C" fn call` versus expected `extern "rust-call"`). The regression test exercises this with `#![feature(fn_traits, unboxed_closures)]`, `struct Foo<T>(T)`, `impl<T: Copy> Fn<()> for Foo<T>`, and flags `-Zpolymorphize=on -Zinline-mir=yes -Zmir-opt-level=0`.
analysis.summary: Historical bug fix in the MIR inliner: before forming a `CallSite`, verify that the instance being inlined has the same ABI as the trait-definition-derived call signature. Without this check, an ABI-incompatible associated function could be inlined, leading the issue's reported `validate_types` index-out-of-bounds ICE under polymorphization/inline-mir. The regression test locks in a normal E0053 diagnostic instead of an ICE.
analysis.trigger: Inlining an associated function whose `InstanceDef::Item` signature has an ABI different from the MIR signature obtained through its trait definition, notably an `extern "C"` `Fn::call` implementation where the trait expects `extern "rust-call"`.
preconditions: MIR inlining is active for the call site, here with `-Zinline-mir=yes` and `-Zmir-opt-level=0` per the regression test.
The instance's own ABI, from `self.tcx.fn_sig(instance_def_id).skip_binder().abi()`, differs from the ABI of the `fn_sig` computed from the called `def_id`.
The reported trigger additionally used `-Zpolymorphize=on`; the fix itself is an inliner ABI compatibility check.
pitfalls: Do not equate matching function signatures with ABI compatibility: the added check specifically compares `instance_fn_sig.abi()` with `fn_sig.abi()`.

Do not derive the checking signature only from the called `def_id`; the historical bug arose while using `self.tcx.fn_sig(def_id)` without also checking `self.tcx.fn_sig(instance_def_id)` for the instance.
Restrict the check to `DefKind::AssocFn`; the patch explicitly uses that def-kind condition before rejecting an ABI mismatch.
A rejected call site must simply not be inlined (`return None`); this fix does not change the call into a different valid callee or rewrite its body.
The regression test is a compile-fail UI test expecting E0053, so an ICE or successful compilation would not validate the historical behavior.

Sharing `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/inline.rs` makes the pass attribution ambiguous between candidate names; this patch's source is the MIR `Inliner`/`CallSite` logic, so attach the knowledge to `Inline`, not automatically to `ForceInline`.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused compile-fail UI test under `tests/ui/mir/` using `// compile-flags: -Zpolymorphize=on -Zinline-mir=yes -Zmir-opt-level=0`, `#![feature(fn_traits, unboxed_closures)]`, and a `Fn` implementation with `extern "C" fn call(&self, _: ()) -> T`. Contrast only the relevant ABI/signature condition between two otherwise identical programs; the expected modern result is the E0053 incompatible-trait-method diagnostic, not an ICE. Check stderr contains `expected "rust-call" fn, found "C" fn` and no `index out of bounds` panic.
evidence: Check that the ABI of the instance we are inlining is correct

When computing the `CallSite` in the mir inliner, double check that the instance of the function that we are inlining is compatible with the signature from the trait definition that we acquire from the MIR.
Additionally, check that the body that we're inlining actually agrees
with the ABI of the trait that the item comes from.
